messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: high error rate on /v1/generate in eu-west-1. Autoscaler observed 3x scale events in 7m; node flapping detected. Pager sent to #oncall.

sara: oncall here, looking. seeing a lot of container crashloops on inference-pool-eu. cpu fine, GPU errors in pod logs.

aj: adding logs — here's a tail from one crash: ```
2026-03-15T09:07:12Z ERROR runtime: kernel launch failed: cudaErrorUnknown: unspecified launch failure
2026-03-15T09:07:12Z FATAL runtime: out of memory while allocating kv-cache for seq=2048
stack: ...
```

mike: autoscaler started 5 nodes, then teardown within 40s each time. likely rapid scale-up/down causing OOM as new pods try to warm KV cache simultaneously.

tanya: customers impacted? any 5xx spikes correlated to SLOs?

sara: yes, external 5xx for gen API at ~15% across eu region for last 9m. hitting SLA error budget for some enterprise customers.

kevin: quick mitigation: pin deployments to a smaller max-scale and disable aggressive burst. I'll patch HPA to stable min=8 max=20 -> min=8 max=12 and set scaleUpCooldown=120s.

aj: +1 for cooldown. also propose temporary circuit-breaker: route low-priority traffic to cheaper variant (gpt-legacy-quant) to reduce startup memory.

ops-bot: deploy request noted: apply hpa change to namespace=redwood-eu, deployment=inference-pool-eu. CI job queued #2789.

sara: performing a manual cordon of the most unstable nodes to stop churn. command: `kubectl cordon node/eu-gpu-spot-5`

mike: while cordoning, I see several pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff with reason 'OOMKilled' and messages referencing seq windows. logs show repeated attempts to allocate ~12GB for attention cache.

aj: trying rollout of patched container with smaller initial cache allocation ENV KV_CACHE_INIT=256 to reduce peak memory on startup. starting canary 2 pods.

tanya: notify affected customers: pinged SalesOps with template. we need to confirm which tenants hit 5xx — adding query to logs.

sara: query run: `SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM request_logs WHERE region='eu' AND status>=500 AND ts>now()-interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY tenant_id` returns 3 high-volume tenants (acct-42, acct-77, acct-101). Notifying CSMs.

kevin: can we temporarily shift scale-policy to prefer node-resident warm pools? maybe increase reserved nodes to reduce cold starts.

mike: launching 4 warm pods pinned to existing stable-gpu-nodes. script: ```bash
for i in 1 2 3 4; do kubectl run warm-$i --image=redwood/inference:stable --limits=memory=12Gi --requests=4Gi --replicas=1; done
```

incident-bot: Incident severity raised to SEV2. Postmortem owner: @sara. Incident channel: #incidents. Incident start: 1825301234.

aj: can confirm canary pods started and stayed up for 180s with no OOM. moving traffic 10% -> canary.

sara: after traffic shift, overall 5xx dropped to 6% then 3%. still above baseline but trending down.

tanya: CSMs acknowledged. prepared customer note: "temporary elevated errors in EU, mitigation in-progress, next update in 30m."

kevin: started autoscaler policy rollback to more conservative thresholds: cpu-target=50% -> 65%, scaleDownDelay=300s. will monitor.
mike: note: we found a Kubernetes bug where rapid pod churn leaves leftover GPU allocations on node until kubelet restart; we also restarted kubelet on 2 nodes.

aj: runbook step executed: `kubectl annotate node <node> redwood/oom-checked=true` to avoid repeat.

sara: preparing handoff for next oncall in 20m. summary: root cause appears to be aggressive autoscaler + heavy cold KV cache allocations triggering OOM on startup which cascaded into node flaps and crashloops. mitigations: 1) HPA cooldown + reduced max, 2) canary with reduced KV_CACHE_INIT, 3) warm pool of pinned pods, 4) kubelet restarts on unstable nodes, 5) routing low-priority traffic to quantized model.

tanya: docs/communication: drafting post to status.redwood.ai -> draft posted, waiting review.

kevin: will follow up with infra to add pre-warm policy to autoscaler: add 'warm_pool_size' parameter and stagger startup to 15s jitter.

incident-bot: scheduled follow-up ops-review in 48h.

sara: handing off to @aj. full context in thread. please monitor for 1h and escalate if >=5% 5xx persists.

aj: taking over. will post updates every 15m. :thumbsup:
